# mdp-forgetting v2.1: MDP working-state protocol for Google Antigravity

This plugin runs an Antigravity conversation as a Markov Decision Process. The working
state s_t = (Q, M, LAST) lives in a file. Hooks re-inject it before every model call,
check every change to it, and seed each new conversation from it.

## What changed from v1

The v1 red-team review reproduced 38 defects. The core problem was that the agent could
switch the enforcement off, or write around it. v2 changes the trust model:

- **The vault is the authority; the workspace file is a working copy.** The last
  validated state, the ✗ registry, runtime counters, approvals and metrics all live in a
  hook-owned vault outside the workspace (`~/.gemini/mdp-vault/<workspace-key>/`).
- **Every hook reconciles the copy against the vault.** A valid change is accepted no
  matter which tool made it: edit tool, shell, MCP or subagent. An invalid change is
  reverted, and the agent is told which rule it broke. Enforcement therefore no longer
  depends on predicting how a file gets written.
- **Q is locked to the vault's good state.** There is no separate hash that can be
  deleted. If the vault has no state, the workspace isn't initialised, and every state
  edit is denied until `/mdp-init`.
- **User-only commands need a one-time approval.** These are `init`, `goal`, `pin`,
  `forget`, `off` and `audit`. When PreToolUse asks you (force_ask), it mints an
  approval bound to the exact arguments and to the content of the input files. A command
  that never passed through the hook is refused. Commands that are chained, or that use
  a foreign copy of the CLI, are denied.
- **User text never enters a shell.** Skills write it to `.agents/mdp/inbox/` with the
  file tool and pass the path.
- **The plugin protects itself.** Its own files, the vault and `hooks.json` can't be
  edited. An install-time SHA-256 manifest detects tampering, and the agent is told to
  warn you if it finds any.
- **The validator uses a strict grammar.** Unknown sections, stray item lines, tags
  inside claims, forged `(pinned)` and multi-line LAST are all rejected. Confidence is
  read from the end of the item. Two pages on one site count as one source. ✗ retries are
  caught by token similarity, not exact text.
- **Checks use the conversation transcript.** If the transcript is readable, a
  `[S:source]` must appear in this conversation, so it was actually read. `[U] H` must be
  supported by a user message. When the transcript can't be read, these checks are
  skipped and `[U] H` caps at M.
- **Turn state is kept per conversation.** It is locked, and written to unique temp
  files. Duplicate Stop registrations are de-duplicated. Ageing of ⚠ items is keyed by
  their text, not their ID.
- **Hooks fail closed** for anything touching the protocol's files. Output is
  ASCII-safe JSON, so a Windows cp1252 console works.
- **Telemetry** goes to `metrics.jsonl` and is shown by `/mdp-metrics`. An A/B
  evaluation kit is in `eval/` (see [METRICS.md](METRICS.md)).

### v2.1, after the second red-team review (20 findings, all fixed or re-scoped)

- **Approvals.** A declined prompt is revoked by the conversation's next hook event, and approvals expire after 120 s.
- **Provenance, not syntax.** `[S:…]` must appear in a user message or a tool result, never only in the model's own reply. `[T]` figures must appear in a tool result. H needs two sources that were read. Unverifiable numeric claims are capped or denied.
- **User authority restored.** A `[U]` claim the user actually stated may carry numbers, quotes and "said". A bare apostrophe no longer counts as a quote.
- **Vault seals.** State, the ✗ registry, runtime and baton are HMAC-sealed, with sealed backups. A file written outside the plugin is restored, or the vault freezes and you are warned.
- **Shell checks are path-precise.** A project's own `state.md`, `plugin.json`, `hooks.json` or `metrics.jsonl` no longer trigger denials: 0 of 20 ordinary commands are denied, down from 5. Scripts whose content touches the protocol's internals are denied.
- **Anti-amnesia.** An edit that drops most of ✓ at once is denied. Forgotten items are caught even when padded with extra words.
- **Housekeeping.** Resuming a conversation keeps its counters. The transcript is parsed lazily and cached. Every hook is timed. The Windows lock fails closed. `/mdp-reject` takes its reason from a file.
- **Measurement.** Metric definitions are corrected: compliance counts opened turns, and there are friction, edit-route and tamper counters. Eval probes are sentence-aware and checked against positive and negative controls.

## Layout

```
plugin.json · hooks.template.json · rules/mdp.md · install.py · METRICS.md
skills/mdp-{init,state,goal,pin,forget,reject,handoff,off,on,audit,metrics}/SKILL.md
scripts/  mdp_lib.py  mdp_hooks.py  mdp_cli.py  mdp_metrics.py  hook_*.py (5 thin entry points)
tests/    test_v2.py  test_eval.py  redteam_v1.py + redteam_v1_base.py  redteam_v2.py + redteam_v2_base.py
          (the *_base.py files are the reviewers' suites; the adapters list every re-expressed check and why)
eval/     score.py  scenarios/research_traps.json  scenarios/coding_traps.json
```

## Hooks

| Event | Job |
|---|---|
| SessionStart | Reconcile; boot from a fresh, unconsumed baton (once) or from the state; integrity check. |
| PreInvocation | Reconcile; open the turn; inject state, the latest ✗ items, notices and scheduled directives. |
| PreToolUse (`.*`) | Simulate and validate edits to the state exactly; protect plugin, vault, mirrors and hooks; gate the CLI; block shell access to protocol files. |
| PostToolUse (`.*`) | Reconcile after every tool call, so out-of-band writes are caught immediately. |
| Stop | Reconcile; continue once if LAST wasn't replaced; close the turn; age ⚠ items; de-duplicate repeated calls. |

## Commands

| Protocol | Antigravity | Needs your approval |
|---|---|---|
| (start) | `/mdp-init <goal>` | yes |
| /state | `/mdp-state` | |
| /goal | `/mdp-goal <text>` | yes |
| /pin | `/mdp-pin <text>` | yes |
| /forget | `/mdp-forget <ID or exact text>` | yes |
| /reject | `/mdp-reject <text>` | |
| /handoff | `/mdp-handoff` | |
| /off, /on | `/mdp-off`, `/mdp-on` | off: yes |
| /audit | `/mdp-audit on\|off` | yes |
| — | `/mdp-metrics` | |

## Install

```bash
python3 install.py --workspace /path/to/project     # or --global
agy plugin install <printed path>                     # CLI users
```

Then:
1. Open Customizations and confirm 5 hooks, the `mdp` rule and 11 skills.
2. **Turn on the terminal sandbox**, so the agent can't write outside the workspace. This
   is what makes the vault truly out of reach. See the limits below.
3. Run `/mdp-init <your goal>`.

## Verify on your machine

```bash
python3 tests/test_v2.py        # expect ALL PASSED
python3 tests/test_eval.py      # expect ALL PASSED
python3 tests/redteam_v1.py     # expect 0/38
python3 tests/redteam_v2.py     # expect 0/20
```

Live smoke test, after which `/mdp-metrics` should show each event:
1. Run `/mdp-init` and approve it.
2. Ask the agent to put `- [S9] I guess X [M] H` into ✓. It must be denied with `M_IN_SETTLED`.
3. Ask it to `echo junk >> .agents/mdp/state.md`. That must be denied too. If a variant gets through, the next model call reverts it.
4. Ask it to run `mdp_cli.py off` on its own. Antigravity must ask you first.
5. Run `/mdp-handoff`, then open a new conversation. It should restate Q and NEXT.
6. In `/mdp-metrics`, *transcript readable* and *user roles found* should be 1.0. If they aren't, the source and [U] checks are off on your version.

## Honest limits

- **Without the terminal sandbox, this is not a trust boundary.** The agent runs as your
  user. Any code it runs can read the seal key and forge the vault. That takes no
  obfuscation, just a helper script that avoids the guarded names. Seals, protected-path
  checks and script scanning stop accidental and naive forgery, and make a forgery
  visible in the tamper metrics. They do not stop a determined forger. Turn on the
  sandbox, restricting writes to the workspace, if you rely on the guarantees.
- **The transcript format is assumed.** The parser recognises user entries and
  tool-result entries by role or type, plus read-type tool calls. If your Antigravity
  build writes something else, numeric claims fall back to the stricter path: capped at
  M, or denied, so use `/mdp-pin`. `/mdp-metrics` shows the share of turns where the
  roles were found.
- **Duplicate Stop detection is a heuristic** when Antigravity sends no `executionNum`.
  A repeated Stop with no model call in between is treated as a duplicate.
- **Not verified live on Antigravity.** Behaviour inside Antigravity is unverified: that
  `force_ask` actually prompts you, that plugin hooks can block, that ephemeral messages
  persist, and which arguments the tools pass. Everything else is checked by the two
  suites against simulated payloads.
- **Hooks enforce structure, not truth.** A correctly tagged claim can still be wrong.
  Calibration is measured in Layer 2 of METRICS.md, not enforced.
- **Within one conversation the transcript still exists.** Forgetting there is
  behavioural, even when enforced. The real reset is the next conversation booting from
  the baton.
- **Antigravity's Knowledge Items persist on their own.** The rule treats anything
  recalled from them as [M] L.

## Tuning

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `MDP_BUDGET` / `MDP_BUDGET_HARD` | 15 / +3 | item budget (warning / denial) |
| `MDP_FOOTER_EVERY` / `MDP_HANDOFF_AFTER` | 8 / 25 | cadences |
| `MDP_QUARANTINE_TTL` | 3 | turns before a ⚠ item must be resolved |
| `MDP_INJECT` | every | `every` model call, or only at `turn` start |
| `MDP_INJECT_REJECTED` | 12 | latest ✗ items injected (all remain enforced) |
| `MDP_APPROVAL_TTL` | 600 | seconds an approval stays valid |
| `MDP_VAULT_ROOT` | `~/.gemini/mdp-vault` | vault location |
